history.user: My sister Imogen had already booked the venue for Mom's retirement dinner before she told any of us. I said I would have liked to be asked, we argued about it for an hour on the phone, and in the end she moved it to a place I suggested.
history.assistant: An hour of arguing, and a dinner you had a hand in. That seems to have mattered.

history.user: It did. I would honestly rather be asked what I think and fight it out than be the one who just goes along. Having a say matters more to me than keeping the peace.
history.assistant: Being asked is the part you would not give up, even at the price of a fight.

history.user: Back from two nights on Pelee Island. The ferry home was so rough that half the deck was green and we sat inside eating crackers.
history.assistant: A rough crossing and a sleeve of crackers. Not the worst way to get home.

steps.text: At dinner tonight Imogen told everyone I am the easiest person in the family, never any fuss. They all laughed and agreed. I know it was meant kindly and I just feel small.
